title: Ashnil Mara Camp Review, From the Riverside Tents to the Crossing Season
meta_title: Ashnil Mara Camp Review: Tents, Meals and River Views
meta_description: Ashnil Mara Camp reviewed: location on the Mara River, tents, what the all-inclusive rate covers, best months and who it suits on a Kenya safari.
excerpt: An honest look at Ashnil Mara Camp on the Mara River: the tents, what is included, the best months to stay and who should book it.
content:
Ashnil Mara Camp is a 30-tent, all-inclusive camp on the banks of the Mara River inside the Masai Mara National Reserve, close to the river crossing points the wildebeest use from roughly July to October. It suits travellers who want comfortable tents, simple logistics and the river on their doorstep rather than a remote private conservancy.

Choosing a Mara camp from brochures is hard, because every listing promises river views and Big Five sightings. This review sets out what Ashnil Mara Camp actually offers according to its own website, where it sits, which months suit it, who will enjoy it and who should look elsewhere, and how it slots into our Kenya safari packages.

Quick Facts

  • Location: On the banks of the Mara River, inside the Masai Mara National Reserve
  • Size: 30 deluxe tents, including interconnecting family tents and tents designed for easier access
  • Meal plan: All-inclusive meals and drinks
  • Getting there: About 45 minutes by air from Nairobi to Keekorok or Ol Kiombo airstrip, or 5-6 hours by road via Narok
  • Facilities: Swimming pool, wellness centre with spa and gym, WiFi, 24-hour solar power
  • Best for: Migration season (July-October), first Mara safaris, families and fly-in trips
  • Open: All year (camp website checked November 2026)

Where Is Ashnil Mara Camp?

Ashnil Mara Camp sits on the Mara River within the Masai Mara National Reserve itself, according to the camp website. Game drives start the moment you leave camp, you pay reserve fees rather than conservancy fees, and the camp describes itself as close to the main river crossing points.

Hippos crowd the river's pools, Nile crocodiles wait on the sandbanks, and in the dry months the water becomes the barrier the herds must cross. Being close to it means less of each morning spent driving and more spent watching.

Getting there by road or by air

By road, the camp is a five to six hour drive from Nairobi through Narok and down into the Great Rift Valley. A pop-up roof 4x4 with your guide is the comfortable way to do it, and it becomes your game drive vehicle on arrival.

Flying is quicker: scheduled light aircraft from Wilson Airport take about 45 minutes, and the camp collects guests from Keekorok and Ol Kiombo airstrips. Expect tight soft-bag luggage limits.

Why a reserve location matters

Staying inside the national reserve has clear upsides: the largest area to explore, short drives to the river, and usually lower nightly rates than private conservancy camps. The trade-off is the rules. Vehicles must stay on the tracks, night drives are not allowed, and at famous crossing points in August you will share the view with other vehicles. Our guide to the Masai Mara reserve versus the conservancies explains the difference in detail.

What Are the Tents Like on the Riverbank?

Ashnil Mara Camp has 30 deluxe tents, each with an en-suite bathroom and hot shower, a walk-in wardrobe, a private sun deck, ceiling fans, a safe and a tea and coffee station. Mosquito nets are provided on request, and the camp runs on 24-hour solar power, so you can charge cameras and phones at any time.

Canvas walls mean you hear the river, hippos grunting at night and, with luck, a lion calling before dawn. Light sleepers should pack earplugs.

Family and accessible tents at Ashnil Mara Camp

Families can book interconnecting tents, so parents and children have their own space with a door between them, and the kitchen prepares special children's meals. Some tents are designed for easier access and the paths are wheelchair-friendly, which is less common than it should be in the Mara and worth knowing if anyone in your party has limited mobility.

The camp website gives no minimum age, so ask about the child policy before you book. As in any unfenced riverside camp, expect guests to be escorted to their tents after dark, and keep a close eye on small children near the water.

WiFi, laundry and the practical details

WiFi is available, the camp offers foreign exchange, and five items of laundry a day are washed free. Check-in is at 12:00 and check-out at 10:00. If your flight out leaves around midday, pack before breakfast so you can fit in one last short drive.

What Is Included in the All-Inclusive Rate?

Ashnil Mara Camp sells its stays as all-inclusive for meals and drinks: the restaurant serves international dishes and African-inspired cooking, and the open-air bar pours wines, spirits, beers and cocktails. Reserve fees, scheduled flights, spa treatments and most special experiences are extra, according to the camp experiences page.

ItemIncluded?What to check
Meals and drinksYesAll meals plus bar drinks; private dining can be arranged
WiFi and laundryYesLaundry is five items a day; extra items are charged
Game drivesDepends on packageSome activities are included in the camp's game package rate; on a Divulge trip your own guide and vehicle are included
Reserve feesNoCharged per person per day, and higher from July to December
Hot air balloonNoBook early for July to October
Spa and massageNoPaid treatments at the wellness centre
Scheduled flightsNoWilson to Keekorok or Ol Kiombo, booked separately or in your package

Reserve fees are often the line people forget. They are charged per person per day and rise in the second half of the year; our Masai Mara entrance fee guide has the current figures. The camp's website lists no room rates, and experience prices are given on request, so any price you see quoted online needs checking against your exact dates.

Between drives, when the animals rest in the midday heat, the pool earns its keep, and the wellness centre adds massage, yoga and a gym that looks over the river.

Which Activities Can You Book From the Camp?

The camp lists daily game drives, nature walks and birdwatching, hot air balloon flights with a champagne bush breakfast, visits to Maasai villages, sundowners, hippo pool breakfasts and barbecue bush dinners. Most guests do two drives a day, or one long full-day drive with a picnic in crossing season.

Hot air balloon over the Mara

Balloons lift off at dawn and drift for about an hour over the plains before landing for breakfast in the bush. In July to October the flights sell out, so book when you confirm your camp. Our Masai Mara balloon safari guide covers launch sites, timings and what the flight is really like.

Walks, hippo pool breakfasts and bush dinners

Guided walks run along the edge of the reserve with an armed ranger, a welcome change after hours in a vehicle. The hippo pool breakfast is served on the riverbank, and bush barbecue dinners can include a Maasai dance.

Photography and Maasai village visits

At Ashnil Mara Camp, keen photographers can take half or full days out with the option of hiring Nikon equipment, which helps if you would rather not fly with a long lens. If photography is the main reason for your trip, our wildlife photography safaris build the days around light and position. Village visits include a talk on Maasai culture and are offered to guests on the camp's ground package; read our post on Maasai village visits and traditions before you go.

When Is the Best Time to Stay at Ashnil Mara Camp?

The best time to stay at Ashnil Mara Camp is July to October, when the migration herds are in the Mara and cross the river close to camp. January to March is the best value window: dry, green after the short rains, quieter, and excellent for big cats, with lower reserve fees than the second half of the year.

MonthsWhat to expect at the riverTrade-offs
January-MarchResident lions, cheetahs, elephants and hippos; short grass makes cats easy to spotCan be hot; no migration herds
April-MayLong rains, lush plains, very few vehiclesMuddy tracks, some afternoon storms; ask whether the camp is offering green season deals
JuneFirst migration columns may arrive late in the monthTiming varies year to year
July-OctoberMigration herds on the plains and crossings on the Mara RiverBusiest and dearest months; balloon and flight seats sell out
November-DecemberHerds head south, short rains freshen the plainsRain showers; Christmas and New Year book up early

No one can promise a crossing on a given day. Herds can mass on the bank for hours and then turn away, so give yourself three nights and at least two full days if crossings are the goal. Our Mara migration timing guide and best time to visit the Masai Mara break the months down further.

Who Will Love This Camp, and Who Should Look Elsewhere?

Ashnil Mara Camp suits first-time Mara visitors, families, honeymooners and anyone who wants a comfortable all-inclusive base near the river crossings without paying conservancy-camp prices. It is less suited to travellers who want walking safaris deep in the bush, night drives or a small camp with very few guests.

A good fit if you

  • want the river and the crossings close by in July to October
  • are travelling with children and need interconnecting tents
  • need easier access tents and paths for someone with limited mobility
  • prefer drinks included rather than a running bar bill
  • are flying in and want a straightforward transfer from the airstrip

Better elsewhere if you

If night drives, off-road tracking of a leopard or long walks are high on your list, a private conservancy such as Mara North Conservancy gives you that freedom. Couples after a tiny, very exclusive camp may find 30 tents too busy. For a side-by-side view of options at every price, see our Masai Mara camps by budget.

How to Fit a Riverside Mara Stay Into Your Kenya Itinerary

Three nights is the right length for most travellers: two full days in the reserve plus arrival and departure. Our 4-day Masai Mara flight safari uses three nights at Ashnil Mara Camp or a similar camp, with flights from Wilson Airport so you lose no time on the road.

For couples, the 7-day Kenya honeymoon safari pairs three nights at Ashnil Mara Camp with three nights on Diani Beach, linked by short flights; it starts from USD 2,850 per adult sharing on low-season rates, with higher prices from July to October and over Christmas. Road travellers often add Lake Nakuru or Lake Naivasha on the way in, which breaks the long drive from Nairobi.

Insider Tips

  • Ask for the river: When you book, ask which tents face the water; the view is the reason to stay on the riverbank
  • Book the balloon early: From July to October, reserve your balloon flight when you confirm the camp
  • Pack soft and light: Light aircraft to Keekorok and Ol Kiombo take soft bags only, with tight weight limits
  • Check your package: Confirm which drives and experiences are included, and whether a village visit is part of it
  • Health: Check the NHS Fit for Travel Kenya page and see a travel clinic about malaria tablets
  • Entry: Apply for your Kenya eTA on the official eTA portal before you fly

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Ashnil Mara Camp inside the Masai Mara National Reserve?

Yes. Ashnil Mara Camp stands on the banks of the Mara River within the Masai Mara National Reserve, so your game drives begin as soon as you leave camp. You pay the reserve's daily fee rather than a private conservancy fee, and the reserve rules apply, which means no night drives and no driving off the tracks.

How do you get to Ashnil Mara Camp from Nairobi?

There are two ways. Scheduled light aircraft from Wilson Airport in Nairobi take about 45 minutes to Keekorok or Ol Kiombo airstrip, and the camp collects guests from both. By road it is a five to six hour drive via Narok and the Rift Valley, usually in a 4x4 safari vehicle with your own guide.

Is Ashnil Mara Camp all-inclusive?

Ashnil Mara Camp says all meals and drinks are included in a stay, including wine, spirits, beer and cocktails at the open-air bar. Reserve fees, scheduled flights, spa treatments and the hot air balloon are charged separately, and which game drives are included depends on the package booked, so check the inclusions line by line.

Is Ashnil Mara Camp good for families?

It is one of the easier Mara camps for families. Ashnil Mara Camp offers interconnecting family tents and special children's meals, and some tents and paths are designed for easier access. The website states no minimum age, so confirm the child policy and any rules near the river before booking with young children.

Can you see the river crossings from Ashnil Mara Camp?

Not reliably from your tent. The camp is close to several Mara River crossing points, but the herds choose where and when to cross, so you drive out with your guide and wait at the river. Crossings mostly happen between July and October, and no camp or operator can promise one on a given day.

Final Thoughts

Ashnil Mara Camp gives you a comfortable, all-inclusive tent on the Mara River, inside the reserve and close to the crossing points, with family tents, a pool and easy flights from Nairobi. Choose it for the river and the migration months; choose a conservancy if you want night drives and fewer vehicles.
